sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive leadership remains firmly entrenched, with Consumer Defensive and Healthcare dominating momentum as cyclical and tech sectors slip.

Market leadership is concentrated in low-beta, non-cyclical areas, with only 2 of 11 sectors qualifying as all-green. Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.933) and Healthcare (momentum 0.883) continue to hold top-tier rankings across all time horizons, while Energy maintains the top YTD rank despite a softer 0.617 momentum score. 

Rotations over the past five sessions showed modest improvements in rate-sensitive and value sectors—Real Estate, Financials, and Utilities all climbed +1 spot—at the direct expense of Technology, Industrials, and Basic Materials, which each slipped -1 spot. Growth and cyclical pockets remain deep laggards, anchored at the bottom by Communication Services (momentum 0.133) and Technology (momentum 0.200).

## Strength
- **Narrow All-Green Breadth:** Just 2 of 11 sectors—Consumer Defensive and Healthcare—are positive across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD frames.
- **Sustained Leadership:** Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.933, rank 2) and Healthcare (momentum 0.883, rank 3) are the only two groups consistently holding top-3 ranks across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- **YTD Anchor:** Energy holds the #1 rank YTD, supported by a solid 0.617 momentum score.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Rate-Sensitive Gains:** Real Estate (rank 4, momentum 0.650), Financials (rank 6, momentum 0.550), and Utilities (rank 8, momentum 0.520) each gained +1 rank position over the last 5 sessions.
- **Cyclical and Tech Slips:** Technology (rank 5, momentum 0.200), Industrials (rank 7, momentum 0.333), and Basic Materials (rank 9, momentum 0.317) all dropped -1 spot over the same period.
- **Bottom-Tier Laggards:** Communication Services remains the weakest overall sector, stuck at rank 11 with a 0.133 momentum score, closely trailed by Consumer Cyclical (rank 10, momentum 0.367).

## Divergences
- **Technology Rank vs. Momentum Disconnect:** Technology holds a mid-tier YTD rank of 5, yet carries the second-lowest momentum score on the board at 0.200.
- **Energy Momentum Fade:** While Energy retains the #1 YTD position, its momentum score (0.617) now trails both Consumer Defensive (0.933) and Healthcare (0.883), as well as Real Estate (0.650).

rotation_phase.label: Defensive
rotation_phase.reasoning: Consumer Defensive and Healthcare are leading as the only all-green sustained momentum sectors while cyclical sectors lag, fitting the classic defensive rotation phase.

- OUT: Industrials -> IN: Real Estate - cyclical weakness (Industrials: -1 spots, wk=-2.6%, mo=-4.8%, rs_slope=-0.356, regime=-0.12) gives way to asset-backed momentum (Real Estate: +1 spots, wk=+0.6%, mo=+3.1%, rs_slope=+0.442, regime=+0.35).
- OUT: Basic Materials -> IN: Financial - lagging commodity exposure (Basic Materials: -1 spots, wk=-0.1%, mo=-8.2%) rotates into value with strong relative strength acceleration (Financial: +1 spots, rs_slope=+0.688, mo=-0.8%).

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Broad defensive strength in Insurance and Retail anchors the market while a sharp tech and hardware sell-off triggers rapid leadership rotation.

Market breadth remains selective, with 28 of 144 groups holding all-green status across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD horizons. Leadership is heavily concentrated in low-volatility sectors—particularly Insurance - Reinsurance (0.916 momentum) and Discount Stores (0.911 momentum). Meanwhile, housing-related cyclicals are mounting a swift short-term rebound, highlighted by 25-spot five-day surges in both Home Improvement Retail and Residential Construction.

Conversely, technology hardware and industrial components are deteriorating rapidly. Semiconductors plunged 28 spots to rank 84 with a momentum score of 0.16, accompanied by steep declines in Electrical Equipment & Parts (-26 spots) and Semiconductor Equipment & Materials (-22 spots). Clean energy and commodity-linked groups anchor the bottom of the market, led by Solar (0.035 momentum) and Uranium (0.043 momentum).

## Strength
- **Insurance Dominance:** Insurance - Reinsurance (momentum 0.92, rank_ytd 9), Insurance Brokers (momentum 0.83), and Insurance - Property & Casualty (momentum 0.83) are all sustained top performers across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- **Consumer Defensive Leadership:** Discount Stores maintains elite positioning as an all-green group with 0.91 momentum (0.911 score, rank_ytd 20), supported by steady demand in Drug Manufacturers - General (momentum 0.84, rank_ytd 16).
- **Core Durables & Health Distribution:** Furnishings, Fixtures & Appliances (momentum 0.87, rank_ytd 24) and Medical Distribution (momentum 0.86, rank_ytd 17) remain firmly entrenched in the top 36 sustained groups.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Housing & Building Rebound:** Home Improvement Retail (+25 spots, rank 74, momentum 0.78), Residential Construction (+25 spots, rank 79, momentum 0.67), and Lumber & Wood Production (+15 spots, rank 58, momentum 0.65) posted the week's strongest relative-rank gains.
- **Tech Hardware Rout:** Heavy selling hit Semiconductors (-28 spots, rank 84, momentum 0.16), Electrical Equipment & Parts (-26 spots, rank 72, momentum 0.17), and Electronic Components (-18 spots, rank 76, momentum 0.21).
- **Entrenched Momentum Laggards:** Solar (momentum 0.035, rank_ytd 143), Uranium (momentum 0.043, rank_ytd 142), and Other Precious Metals & Mining (momentum 0.054, rank_ytd 141) remain the weakest groups across the broader market.

## Divergences
- **Fading High-Momentum Groups:** Lodging (momentum 0.77, rank -4 over 5d) and Beverages - Non-Alcoholic (momentum 0.75, rank -2 over 5d) are exhibiting early momentum erosion despite strong broader profiles.
- **Emerging Low-Momentum Turnarounds:** Building Products & Equipment jumped 9 spots over 5 days despite a lower momentum score of 0.41, while Banks - Regional gained 5 spots with a 0.50 momentum reading.

- OUT: Electrical Equipment & Parts -> IN: Residential Construction - Building-related capital shifted from industrial electrical suppliers (-26 spots, wk=-7.9%, mo=-19.1%) directly into homebuilders surging to leadership (+25 spots, wk=+6.9%, regime=+0.37).
